correctness.rationale: The tree filtration rule yields an arrow precisely when one earlier neighbor exists. Every root-first filtration produces N-1 pairs; any N-1 matching exhausts edges and has a unique sink, hence exactly a rooted orientation. Direct star/double-star root selection handles all smaller diameters; a four-edge geodesic and order v0,v4,v1,v3 force arrows with disjoint root components for every larger diameter. Every such face extends to an inclusion-maximal lower face. The finite checker independently enumerates vertex orders for 1,470 labeled trees. The strong-collapse consequence is already established for the equal ordinary pure complex (Donovan--Lin--Scoville Proposition 18), and no computational extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the exact all-tree purity iff threshold for the filtration-defined strong complex, including nonpath diameter-four obstructions and double-star positive cases. The 2026 primary source treats paths and stars; older papers treat ordinary Morse complexes and their pure part, not this strong-complex purity criterion. The older strong collapsibility result is explicitly credited, never claimed as new. The mathematical implication comparisons and residual risks follow.

value.rationale: A sharp all-tree characterization of purity for a newly studied filtration-generated topological complex gives the exact diameter boundary, settles every branching double star and extends the known four-edge-path obstruction to arbitrary branching trees. Purity controls whether the full strong complex reduces to the established collapsible pure Morse core; the criterion isolates an intrinsic graph parameter rather than an arbitrary finite calculation. The ordinary pure collapse is correctly identified as old work.
